data.prompt:
Fleet: online-inference pods on a shared GPU cluster. Snapshot (admission) day: 143.
Billing window: one month = 730 hours; annualise by multiplying the month by 12.

Right-sizing policy (apply to every pod, in this order):
1. History. A workload's eligible history is its rows in the history table with
   day in [136, 142] (the 7 days before the snapshot day; rows on or
   after the snapshot day were not finished before admission and rows older than 7 days are stale).
   A pod is WARM if it has a workload_id with at least 3 eligible rows; otherwise it is COLD
   (including pods with an empty workload_id).
2. Base need (GPUs). WARM: the nearest-rank P90 of the eligible need_gpu values (sort ascending and take
   the ceil(0.9*n)-th value, 1-indexed). COLD: cold_fraction(model_type, gpu_type) x gpu_request.
3. Safety margin. need = base x (1 + margin(model_type, WARM/COLD)). Use exact arithmetic.
4. Slice. If need >= gpu_request, allocate gpu_request. Otherwise, if need <= 1, allocate the smallest
   slice in the grid [0.1, 0.2, 0.25, 0.3, 0.4, 0.5, 0.7, 1] that is >= need; if need > 1, allocate ceil(need) whole GPUs.
   Never allocate more than gpu_request.
5. Readiness veto. If the allocation is smaller than gpu_request, the shrink adds
   sensitivity(gpu_type) x (gpu_request - allocation) / gpu_request percentage points of
   failure-to-ready risk. If ready_risk_pct + added risk > 50, veto the shrink: allocate gpu_request
   and list the pod as vetoed. A pod whose step-4 allocation already equals gpu_request is not vetoed.
6. Fleet totals. reserved_gpu_hours = sum(gpu_request x hours). reclaimed_gpu_hours =
   sum((gpu_request - allocation) x hours). reclaim_pct = 100 x reclaimed / reserved, rounded half-up
   to 2 decimals. annual_savings_usd = 12 x sum((gpu_request - allocation) x hours x price(gpu_type)),
   rounded half-up to the cent.

Fleet: online-inference pods on a shared GPU cluster. Snapshot (admission) day: 71.
Billing window: one month = 730 hours; annualise by multiplying the month by 12.

Right-sizing policy (apply to every pod, in this order):
1. History. A workload's eligible history is its rows in the history table with
   day in [64, 70] (the 7 days before the snapshot day; rows on or
   after the snapshot day were not finished before admission and rows older than 7 days are stale).
   A pod is WARM if it has a workload_id with at least 3 eligible rows; otherwise it is COLD
   (including pods with an empty workload_id).
2. Base need (GPUs). WARM: the nearest-rank P90 of the eligible need_gpu values (sort ascending and take
   the ceil(0.9*n)-th value, 1-indexed). COLD: cold_fraction(model_type, gpu_type) x gpu_request.
3. Safety margin. need = base x (1 + margin(model_type, WARM/COLD)). Use exact arithmetic.
4. Slice. If need >= gpu_request, allocate gpu_request. Otherwise, if need <= 1, allocate the smallest
   slice in the grid [0.1, 0.2, 0.25, 0.3, 0.4, 0.5, 0.7, 1] that is >= need; if need > 1, allocate ceil(need) whole GPUs.
   Never allocate more than gpu_request.
5. Readiness veto. If the allocation is smaller than gpu_request, the shrink adds
   sensitivity(gpu_type) x (gpu_request - allocation) / gpu_request percentage points of
   failure-to-ready risk. If ready_risk_pct + added risk > 50, veto the shrink: allocate gpu_request

data.prompt:
Fleet: online-inference pods on a shared GPU cluster. Snapshot (admission) day: 83.
Billing window: one month = 730 hours; annualise by multiplying the month by 12.

Right-sizing policy (apply to every pod, in this order):
1. History. A workload's eligible history is its rows in the history table with
   day in [76, 82] (the 7 days before the snapshot day; rows on or
   after the snapshot day were not finished before admission and rows older than 7 days are stale).
   A pod is WARM if it has a workload_id with at least 3 eligible rows; otherwise it is COLD
   (including pods with an empty workload_id).
2. Base need (GPUs). WARM: the nearest-rank P90 of the eligible need_gpu values (sort ascending and take
   the ceil(0.9*n)-th value, 1-indexed). COLD: cold_fraction(model_type, gpu_type) x gpu_request.
3. Safety margin. need = base x (1 + margin(model_type, WARM/COLD)). Use exact arithmetic.
4. Slice. If need >= gpu_request, allocate gpu_request. Otherwise, if need <= 1, allocate the smallest
   slice in the grid [0.1, 0.2, 0.25, 0.3, 0.4, 0.5, 0.7, 1] that is >= need; if need > 1, allocate ceil(need) whole GPUs.
   Never allocate more than gpu_request.
5. Readiness veto. If the allocation is smaller than gpu_request, the shrink adds
   sensitivity(gpu_type) x (gpu_request - allocation) / gpu_request percentage points of
   failure-to-ready risk. If ready_risk_pct + added risk > 50, veto the shrink: allocate gpu_request
   and list the pod as vetoed. A pod whose step-4 allocation already equals gpu_request is not vetoed.
6. Fleet totals. reserved_gpu_hours = sum(gpu_request x hours). reclaimed_gpu_hours =
   sum((gpu_request - allocation) x hours). reclaim_pct = 100 x reclaimed / reserved, rounded half-up
   to 2 decimals. annual_savings_usd = 12 x sum((gpu_request - allocation) x hours x price(gpu_type)),

Fleet: online-inference pods on a shared GPU cluster. Snapshot (admission) day: 132.
Billing window: one month = 730 hours; annualise by multiplying the month by 12.

Right-sizing policy (apply to every pod, in this order):
1. History. A workload's eligible history is its rows in the history table with
   day in [125, 131] (the 7 days before the snapshot day; rows on or
   after the snapshot day were not finished before admission and rows older than 7 days are stale).
   A pod is WARM if it has a workload_id with at least 3 eligible rows; otherwise it is COLD
   (including pods with an empty workload_id).
2. Base need (GPUs). WARM: the nearest-rank P90 of the eligible need_gpu values (sort ascending and take
   the ceil(0.9*n)-th value, 1-indexed). COLD: cold_fraction(model_type, gpu_type) x gpu_request.
3. Safety margin. need = base x (1 + margin(model_type, WARM/COLD)). Use exact arithmetic.
4. Slice. If need >= gpu_request, allocate gpu_request. Otherwise, if need <= 1, allocate the smallest
   slice in the grid [0.1, 0.2, 0.25, 0.3, 0.4, 0.5, 0.7, 1] that is >= need; if need > 1, allocate ceil(need) whole GPUs.
   Never allocate more than gpu_request.
5. Readiness veto. If the allocation is smaller than gpu_request, the shrink adds
   sensitivity(gpu_type) x (gpu_request - allocation) / gpu_request percentage points of
   failure-to-ready risk. If ready_risk_pct + added risk > 50, veto the shrink: allocate gpu_request
   and list the pod as vetoed. A pod whose step-4 allocation already equals gpu_request is not vetoed.
6. Fleet totals. reserved_gpu_hours = sum(gpu_request x hours). reclaimed_gpu_hours =
   sum((gpu_request - allocation) x hours). reclaim_pct = 100 x reclaimed / reserved, rounded half-up

data.prompt:
Fleet: online-inference pods on a shared GPU cluster. Snapshot (admission) day: 116.
Billing window: one month = 730 hours; annualise by multiplying the month by 12.

Right-sizing policy (apply to every pod, in this order):
1. History. A workload's eligible history is its rows in the history table with
   day in [109, 115] (the 7 days before the snapshot day; rows on or
   after the snapshot day were not finished before admission and rows older than 7 days are stale).
   A pod is WARM if it has a workload_id with at least 3 eligible rows; otherwise it is COLD
   (including pods with an empty workload_id).
2. Base need (GPUs). WARM: the nearest-rank P90 of the eligible need_gpu values (sort ascending and take
   the ceil(0.9*n)-th value, 1-indexed). COLD: cold_fraction(model_type, gpu_type) x gpu_request.
3. Safety margin. need = base x (1 + margin(model_type, WARM/COLD)). Use exact arithmetic.
4. Slice. If need >= gpu_request, allocate gpu_request. Otherwise, if need <= 1, allocate the smallest
   slice in the grid [0.1, 0.2, 0.25, 0.3, 0.4, 0.5, 0.7, 1] that is >= need; if need > 1, allocate ceil(need) whole GPUs.
   Never allocate more than gpu_request.
5. Readiness veto. If the allocation is smaller than gpu_request, the shrink adds
   sensitivity(gpu_type) x (gpu_request - allocation) / gpu_request percentage points of
   failure-to-ready risk. If ready_risk_pct + added risk > 50, veto the shrink: allocate gpu_request
   and list the pod as vetoed. A pod whose step-4 allocation already equals gpu_request is not vetoed.
6. Fleet totals. reserved_gpu_hours = sum(gpu_request x hours). reclaimed_gpu_hours =
   sum((gpu_request - allocation) x hours). reclaim_pct = 100 x reclaimed / reserved, rounded half-up
   to 2 decimals. annual_savings_usd = 12 x sum((gpu_request - allocation) x hours x price(gpu_type)),

data.prompt:
Fleet: online-inference pods on a shared GPU cluster. Snapshot (admission) day: 86.
Billing window: one month = 730 hours; annualise by multiplying the month by 12.

Right-sizing policy (apply to every pod, in this order):
1. History. A workload's eligible history is its rows in the history table with
   day in [79, 85] (the 7 days before the snapshot day; rows on or
   after the snapshot day were not finished before admission and rows older than 7 days are stale).
   A pod is WARM if it has a workload_id with at least 3 eligible rows; otherwise it is COLD
   (including pods with an empty workload_id).
2. Base need (GPUs). WARM: the nearest-rank P90 of the eligible need_gpu values (sort ascending and take
   the ceil(0.9*n)-th value, 1-indexed). COLD: cold_fraction(model_type, gpu_type) x gpu_request.
3. Safety margin. need = base x (1 + margin(model_type, WARM/COLD)). Use exact arithmetic.
4. Slice. If need >= gpu_request, allocate gpu_request. Otherwise, if need <= 1, allocate the smallest
   slice in the grid [0.1, 0.2, 0.25, 0.3, 0.4, 0.5, 0.7, 1] that is >= need; if need > 1, allocate ceil(need) whole GPUs.
   Never allocate more than gpu_request.
5. Readiness veto. If the allocation is smaller than gpu_request, the shrink adds
   sensitivity(gpu_type) x (gpu_request - allocation) / gpu_request percentage points of
   failure-to-ready risk. If ready_risk_pct + added risk > 50, veto the shrink: allocate gpu_request
   and list the pod as vetoed. A pod whose step-4 allocation already equals gpu_request is not vetoed.
6. Fleet totals. reserved_gpu_hours = sum(gpu_request x hours). reclaimed_gpu_hours =
   sum((gpu_request - allocation) x hours). reclaim_pct = 100 x reclaimed / reserved, rounded half-up

data.prompt:
Fleet: online-inference pods on a shared GPU cluster. Snapshot (admission) day: 98.
Billing window: one month = 730 hours; annualise by multiplying the month by 12.

Right-sizing policy (apply to every pod, in this order):
1. History. A workload's eligible history is its rows in the history table with
   day in [91, 97] (the 7 days before the snapshot day; rows on or
   after the snapshot day were not finished before admission and rows older than 7 days are stale).
   A pod is WARM if it has a workload_id with at least 3 eligible rows; otherwise it is COLD
   (including pods with an empty workload_id).
2. Base need (GPUs). WARM: the nearest-rank P90 of the eligible need_gpu values (sort ascending and take
   the ceil(0.9*n)-th value, 1-indexed). COLD: cold_fraction(model_type, gpu_type) x gpu_request.
3. Safety margin. need = base x (1 + margin(model_type, WARM/COLD)). Use exact arithmetic.
4. Slice. If need >= gpu_request, allocate gpu_request. Otherwise, if need <= 1, allocate the smallest
   slice in the grid [0.1, 0.2, 0.25, 0.3, 0.4, 0.5, 0.7, 1] that is >= need; if need > 1, allocate ceil(need) whole GPUs.
   Never allocate more than gpu_request.
5. Readiness veto. If the allocation is smaller than gpu_request, the shrink adds
   sensitivity(gpu_type) x (gpu_request - allocation) / gpu_request percentage points of
   failure-to-ready risk. If ready_risk_pct + added risk > 50, veto the shrink: allocate gpu_request
   and list the pod as vetoed. A pod whose step-4 allocation already equals gpu_request is not vetoed.
6. Fleet totals. reserved_gpu_hours = sum(gpu_request x hours). reclaimed_gpu_hours =
   sum((gpu_request - allocation) x hours). reclaim_pct = 100 x reclaimed / reserved, rounded half-up

Fleet: online-inference pods on a shared GPU cluster. Snapshot (admission) day: 82.
Billing window: one month = 730 hours; annualise by multiplying the month by 12.

Right-sizing policy (apply to every pod, in this order):
1. History. A workload's eligible history is its rows in the history table with
   day in [75, 81] (the 7 days before the snapshot day; rows on or
   after the snapshot day were not finished before admission and rows older than 7 days are stale).
   A pod is WARM if it has a workload_id with at least 3 eligible rows; otherwise it is COLD
   (including pods with an empty workload_id).
2. Base need (GPUs). WARM: the nearest-rank P90 of the eligible need_gpu values (sort ascending and take
   the ceil(0.9*n)-th value, 1-indexed). COLD: cold_fraction(model_type, gpu_type) x gpu_request.
3. Safety margin. need = base x (1 + margin(model_type, WARM/COLD)). Use exact arithmetic.
4. Slice. If need >= gpu_request, allocate gpu_request. Otherwise, if need <= 1, allocate the smallest
   slice in the grid [0.1, 0.2, 0.25, 0.3, 0.4, 0.5, 0.7, 1] that is >= need; if need > 1, allocate ceil(need) whole GPUs.
   Never allocate more than gpu_request.
5. Readiness veto. If the allocation is smaller than gpu_request, the shrink adds
   sensitivity(gpu_type) x (gpu_request - allocation) / gpu_request percentage points of
   failure-to-ready risk. If ready_risk_pct + added risk > 50, veto the shrink: allocate gpu_request
   and list the pod as vetoed. A pod whose step-4 allocation already equals gpu_request is not vetoed.
6. Fleet totals. reserved_gpu_hours = sum(gpu_request x hours). reclaimed_gpu_hours =
   sum((gpu_request - allocation) x hours). reclaim_pct = 100 x reclaimed / reserved, rounded half-up

data.prompt:
Fleet: online-inference pods on a shared GPU cluster. Snapshot (admission) day: 156.
Billing window: one month = 730 hours; annualise by multiplying the month by 12.

Right-sizing policy (apply to every pod, in this order):
1. History. A workload's eligible history is its rows in the history table with
   day in [149, 155] (the 7 days before the snapshot day; rows on or
   after the snapshot day were not finished before admission and rows older than 7 days are stale).
   A pod is WARM if it has a workload_id with at least 3 eligible rows; otherwise it is COLD
   (including pods with an empty workload_id).
2. Base need (GPUs). WARM: the nearest-rank P90 of the eligible need_gpu values (sort ascending and take
   the ceil(0.9*n)-th value, 1-indexed). COLD: cold_fraction(model_type, gpu_type) x gpu_request.
3. Safety margin. need = base x (1 + margin(model_type, WARM/COLD)). Use exact arithmetic.
4. Slice. If need >= gpu_request, allocate gpu_request. Otherwise, if need <= 1, allocate the smallest
   slice in the grid [0.1, 0.2, 0.25, 0.3, 0.4, 0.5, 0.7, 1] that is >= need; if need > 1, allocate ceil(need) whole GPUs.
   Never allocate more than gpu_request.
5. Readiness veto. If the allocation is smaller than gpu_request, the shrink adds
   sensitivity(gpu_type) x (gpu_request - allocation) / gpu_request percentage points of
   failure-to-ready risk. If ready_risk_pct + added risk > 50, veto the shrink: allocate gpu_request
   and list the pod as vetoed. A pod whose step-4 allocation already equals gpu_request is not vetoed.
6. Fleet totals. reserved_gpu_hours = sum(gpu_request x hours). reclaimed_gpu_hours =
   sum((gpu_request - allocation) x hours). reclaim_pct = 100 x reclaimed / reserved, rounded half-up
   to 2 decimals. annual_savings_usd = 12 x sum((gpu_request - allocation) x hours x price(gpu_type)),
   rounded half-up to the cent.

   the ceil(0.9*n)-th value, 1-indexed). COLD: cold_fraction(model_type, gpu_type) x gpu_request.
3. Safety margin. need = base x (1 + margin(model_type, WARM/COLD)). Use exact arithmetic.

the policy exactly, then report the fleet totals. Think as needed, then finish with exactly one block:

Fleet: online-inference pods on a shared GPU cluster. Snapshot (admission) day: 62.
Billing window: one month = 730 hours; annualise by multiplying the month by 12.

Right-sizing policy (apply to every pod, in this order):
1. History. A workload's eligible history is its rows in the history table with
   day in [55, 61] (the 7 days before the snapshot day; rows on or
   after the snapshot day were not finished before admission and rows older than 7 days are stale).
   A pod is WARM if it has a workload_id with at least 3 eligible rows; otherwise it is COLD
   (including pods with an empty workload_id).
2. Base need (GPUs). WARM: the nearest-rank P90 of the eligible need_gpu values (sort ascending and take
   the ceil(0.9*n)-th value, 1-indexed). COLD: cold_fraction(model_type, gpu_type) x gpu_request.
3. Safety margin. need = base x (1 + margin(model_type, WARM/COLD)). Use exact arithmetic.
4. Slice. If need >= gpu_request, allocate gpu_request. Otherwise, if need <= 1, allocate the smallest
   slice in the grid [0.1, 0.2, 0.25, 0.3, 0.4, 0.5, 0.7, 1] that is >= need; if need > 1, allocate ceil(need) whole GPUs.
   Never allocate more than gpu_request.
5. Readiness veto. If the allocation is smaller than gpu_request, the shrink adds
   sensitivity(gpu_type) x (gpu_request - allocation) / gpu_request percentage points of
   failure-to-ready risk. If ready_risk_pct + added risk > 50, veto the shrink: allocate gpu_request
   and list the pod as vetoed. A pod whose step-4 allocation already equals gpu_request is not vetoed.
6. Fleet totals. reserved_gpu_hours = sum(gpu_request x hours). reclaimed_gpu_hours =
   sum((gpu_request - allocation) x hours). reclaim_pct = 100 x reclaimed / reserved, rounded half-up
   to 2 decimals. annual_savings_usd = 12 x sum((gpu_request - allocation) x hours x price(gpu_type)),

Fleet: online-inference pods on a shared GPU cluster. Snapshot (admission) day: 157.
Billing window: one month = 730 hours; annualise by multiplying the month by 12.

Right-sizing policy (apply to every pod, in this order):
1. History. A workload's eligible history is its rows in the history table with
   day in [150, 156] (the 7 days before the snapshot day; rows on or
   after the snapshot day were not finished before admission and rows older than 7 days are stale).
   A pod is WARM if it has a workload_id with at least 3 eligible rows; otherwise it is COLD
   (including pods with an empty workload_id).
2. Base need (GPUs). WARM: the nearest-rank P90 of the eligible need_gpu values (sort ascending and take
   the ceil(0.9*n)-th value, 1-indexed). COLD: cold_fraction(model_type, gpu_type) x gpu_request.
3. Safety margin. need = base x (1 + margin(model_type, WARM/COLD)). Use exact arithmetic.
4. Slice. If need >= gpu_request, allocate gpu_request. Otherwise, if need <= 1, allocate the smallest
   slice in the grid [0.1, 0.2, 0.25, 0.3, 0.4, 0.5, 0.7, 1] that is >= need; if need > 1, allocate ceil(need) whole GPUs.

5. Readiness veto. If the allocation is smaller than gpu_request, the shrink adds
   sensitivity(gpu_type) x (gpu_request - allocation) / gpu_request percentage points of

message.content:
You are a GPU capacity engineer. Right-size every online-inference pod in the fleet snapshot by applying
the policy exactly, then report the fleet totals. Think as needed, then finish with exactly one block:
<answer>
{"allocations": {"pod_01": 0.4, "pod_02": 2}, "vetoed": ["pod_07"],
 "reserved_gpu_hours": 0.00, "reclaimed_gpu_hours": 0.00, "reclaim_pct": 0.00, "annual_savings_usd": 0.00}
</answer>
Give an allocation (in GPUs) for every pod. "vetoed" lists only pods whose shrink the readiness veto blocked.

Fleet: online-inference pods on a shared GPU cluster. Snapshot (admission) day: 161.
Billing window: one month = 730 hours; annualise by multiplying the month by 12.

Right-sizing policy (apply to every pod, in this order):
1. History. A workload's eligible history is its rows in the history table with
   day in [154, 160] (the 7 days before the snapshot day; rows on or
   after the snapshot day were not finished before admission and rows older than 7 days are stale).
   A pod is WARM if it has a workload_id with at least 3 eligible rows; otherwise it is COLD
   (including pods with an empty workload_id).
2. Base need (GPUs). WARM: the nearest-rank P90 of the eligible need_gpu values (sort ascending and take
   the ceil(0.9*n)-th value, 1-indexed). COLD: cold_fraction(model_type, gpu_type) x gpu_request.
3. Safety margin. need = base x (1 + margin(model_type, WARM/COLD)). Use exact arithmetic.
4. Slice. If need >= gpu_request, allocate gpu_request. Otherwise, if need <= 1, allocate the smallest
   slice in the grid [0.1, 0.2, 0.25, 0.3, 0.4, 0.5, 0.7, 1] that is >= need; if need > 1, allocate ceil(need) whole GPUs.
   Never allocate more than gpu_request.
5. Readiness veto. If the allocation is smaller than gpu_request, the shrink adds
   sensitivity(gpu_type) x (gpu_request - allocation) / gpu_request percentage points of
   failure-to-ready risk. If ready_risk_pct + added risk > 50, veto the shrink: allocate gpu_request
   and list the pod as vetoed. A pod whose step-4 allocation already equals gpu_request is not vetoed.
6. Fleet totals. reserved_gpu_hours = sum(gpu_request x hours). reclaimed_gpu_hours =
   sum((gpu_request - allocation) x hours). reclaim_pct = 100 x reclaimed / reserved, rounded half-up
   to 2 decimals. annual_savings_usd = 12 x sum((gpu_request - allocation) x hours x price(gpu_type)),
   rounded half-up to the cent.
